name: Kettlebell Curl
description: The kettlebell curl uses a kettlebell's offset center of mass, which hangs below the handle, creating a different lever and tension pattern than dumbbells. At the bottom of the curl, the hanging bell creates more tension than a dumbbell at the same arm position. The kettlebell can be held by the handle for a neutral-to-supinated curl or by the horns for a supinated grip curl, offering useful variation.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding one or two kettlebells by the handle. Arms extended at sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Hold by the handle for a neutral/supinated curl. Can hold by the horns for more supination.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended, kettlebell(s) hanging.
Step 2: Curl the kettlebell(s) upward by flexing the elbows, supinating the grip as you curl.
Step 3: Curl until maximum elbow flexion.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
safety_considerations: The offset weight can torque the wrist — control the bell
coaching_cues: Let the bell hang — control it
